## <span style="color:  #276d6c;"> `r fontawesome::fa("user", fill = "#276d6c", prefer_type="solid")` Bio</span>
|  |  
|:--------------------------------------------------|
I am a PhD student in the **<a href="https://publichealth.jhu.edu/departments/population-family-and-reproductive-health/people/students/phd-students"><span style="color:#ae2e2e;">Department of Population, Family, and Reproductive Health</span></a>**,  at the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health. My research focuses on maternal and child health, with particular interests in nutrition, epigenetic aging, and the developmental origins of health and disease (DOHaD). I have experience working with international research consortia and large-scale cohort studies, including projects on nutrition and epigenetic aging acceleration, gestational weight gain, indoor air pollution, and global pandemic preparedness.
<br>
My long-term goal is to bridge research and policy by designing and analyzing studies that inform interventions and strategies to improve women’s health worldwide.
<br>
